prose: Wired reads Character.AI's Chapter 11 filings and concludes the bankruptcy was not a collapse but a deal mechanism. The two-part structure lets Disney hire most of Character.AI's staff - including now-former CEO Karandeep Anand - and potentially acquire most of its technology, while insulating Disney from the startup's mounting legal liabilities: multiple private lawsuits over chatbot safety and investigations by regulators around the world. In a court declaration, Character.AI's newly appointed CEO said the bankruptcy's goal was a 'consensual resolution' with personal-injury claimants and the investigating states while maximizing asset value for shareholders. Whatever remains of Character.AI keeps the liabilities; Disney gets the talent and tech. The filings make the arrangement - bankruptcy as a get-out-of-lawsuits card - unusually explicit.
highlights: Character.AI's Chapter 11 is structured as part of a two-part Disney deal, per court filings
Disney hires most of the staff, including former CEO Karandeep Anand
Disney may acquire most of the technology while avoiding the startup's legal liabilities
Character.AI faces multiple chatbot-safety lawsuits and regulator investigations
New CEO's declaration: goal is a 'consensual resolution' with claimants and states
The remaining shell keeps the liabilities; Wired calls it bankruptcy as a get-out-of-lawsuits card
